correctness.rationale: Every update reduces to the two nonhub counts and two bridge hub bits; all odd cliques freeze by step two, and even cliques either immediately homogenize or occupy one of two critical states where all nonhubs flip and the hub copies its neighbor. Persistent criticality occurs exactly for both-even opposite hub states, and backward criticality shows no transient enters a cycle. The sharp transient bounds 2,4,5 follow by local stabilization case analysis and are attained by parameterized witnesses. Binomial choices count labelled two-cycles. Finite independent direct enumeration tested 170688 initial configurations on 21 small size pairs; compressed weighted checking tested 2304 ordered parameter pairs and witnesses 9604. These checks corroborate an explicit all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The new exact classification concerns a deterministic bridge-connected pair of cliques with sharp three-way parity-dependent transient times, a binomial count of primitive two-cycles, and a proof their basins consist solely of periodic states. Neither the 1980 general period restriction, the 2014 unimodular/random majority theory, nor the 2015 clique-module voting-time bound implies these enumerative and sharp values. Published findings and previous-claim comparisons found no covering claim. Unindexed equivalence remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: Bridge barbells are canonical weakly coupled dense communities. The result gives complete asymptotic regime classification and a sharp parameter-independent settling bound, isolates rare parity-locked cycles inaccessible from transients, and computes their exact labelled count and asymptotic probability 1/(pi sqrt(mn)). This distinguishes robust community disagreement from true nonconvergent oscillation in a natural infinite-family setting, beyond the general period-two theorem.
